newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks stable ahead of Christmas lull.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks stable ahead of Christmas lull.

text.p: Croatian stocks were stable to higher on lower volume and turnover on Wednesday and analysts predicted the festive season lull would slow down the trading.
"The calm before (Christmas) holidays has already set in," said Marijana Reskovac of Karlovacka Banka, adding investor interest now lay elsewhere.
She said some trading, if any, might be made with the fully listed Zagrebacka Banka and drugs firm Pliva in the last weeks of 1996.
Some brokers already said they would close down around Christmas, she said.
Two of six traded issues rose, three were flat and one fell. Volume was lower at 7,095 shares, turnover also down at 7.1 million kuna.
Top gainer hotelier Istraturist inched up five kuna to 130, with 175 shares changing hands. Confectioner Kras also added five kuna to 410, with 70 units sold.
The most actively traded, Zagrebacka Banka, was the only loser, edging down 10 kuna to 980, on volume of 6,264 shares. Its E-series was flat at 430 kuna, with 220 shares traded.
Pliva and food processor Podravka both remained unchanged at 13,000 and 207 kuna respectively. Pliva sold 53 shares and Podravka 313.

The first issue of public debt refinancing bonds traded at 96.59 of face value, on turnover of 1.5 million kuna. Second tranche traded at 7.10 above par, down from 7.50 on Tuesday on turnover of 1.9 million kuna.
